source_title: Govt plans to rate national highway corridors on safety, road quality
source_excerpt: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is planning to rank national highway (NHs) corridors based on their performance, to identify deficiencies and measures for improvement, a circular on Thursday said. Two separate rating criteria will be adopted for Access Controlled Expressways, Designated High-Speed Corridors and Normal National Highways. The move comes as the ministry is redoing its contractual provisions for engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) projects, increasing accountability for deficiencies and accident-prone spots. It has also begun internally rating highway contractors and linked several financial obligations to these ratings. The NH corridor rating framework comprises three categories — Highway Efficiency, Highway Safety, and User Experience — with various parameters under each category. The framework will measure peak congestion as the ratio of maximum of peak hour traffic over five consecutive days during peak season to hourly design capacity, along with level of service across the stretch. However, the highest weightage in this rating methodology has been given to the condition of the road, measured through the pavement condition index (PCI), which will be evaluated by a network survey vehicle (NSV). The ratings will also take into account the frequency of wayside amenities, toll plaza rating, and presence of Advanced Traffic Management Systems (ATMS). From a safety perspective, the ratings will take into account the frequency of accidents per annum per 10 kilometres, failure in the project leading to closures, number of fatalities in accidents, and the severity of the accidents. The ministry has increasingly faced criticism in the past over the poor condition of highways. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari earlier this week encouraged such complaints, saying that it enables him to straighten out the officials and contractors responsible for the errors.
